stimulus.text: "The sixteen years of Jefferson and Madison's rule furnished international tests of popular intelligence upon which Americans could depend. … Yet the Americans developed, in the course of twenty years, a surprising degree of skill in naval affairs. … Not only were American vessels better in model, faster in sailing … but they were also better equipped." —Henry Adams, History of the United States During the Administrations of Thomas Jefferson and James Madison, 1889–1891 (abridged)

parts: A. Briefly describe Adams's perspective on the American navy during the War of 1812 era.
B. Briefly explain ONE historical event or development that supports Adams's perspective.
C. Briefly explain ONE historical event or development that challenges Adams's perspective.
exemplar: Adams argues that despite starting with fewer ships, resources, and experience than Britain, France, or Spain, the United States developed surprising naval skill, building faster, better-handled, and better-equipped vessels.
The USS Constitution's victories over HMS Guerriere and HMS Java in 1812 support Adams: single American frigates repeatedly defeated comparable British warships.
The British naval blockade of the American coast devastated U.S. trade and bottled up the tiny American fleet, showing the limits of American naval power against Britain's overwhelming numbers.

stimulus.text:
"We, whose names are underwritten, the Loyal Subjects of our dread Sovereign Lord King James... Having undertaken for the Glory of God, and Advancement of the Christian Faith, and the Honour of our King and Country, a Voyage to plant the first Colony in the northern Parts of Virginia; Do by these Presents, solemnly and mutually, in the Presence of God and one another, covenant and combine ourselves together into a civil Body Politick, for our better Ordering and Preservation..."
—Mayflower Compact, 1620

parts: A. Briefly explain what the signers of the Mayflower Compact intended to accomplish.
B. Briefly explain ONE reason English colonies in the New World proved successful.
C. Briefly explain ONE advantage enjoyed by the rival French colonies.
exemplar: The signers intended to create a legitimate civil government even though they had landed outside the bounds of their Virginia charter. By 'covenant and combine ourselves together into a civil Body Politick,' they agreed to make and obey laws for the colony's 'better Ordering and Preservation.'

One reason English colonies succeeded was their early practice of self-government. Virginia's House of Burgesses (1619) gave settlers a voice in their affairs, drawing more migrants and defusing conflict with authority.

The French enjoyed the advantage of strong Native alliances. Because their fur-trade empire depended on Native hunters and middlemen, the French built partnerships rather than seizing farmland, sparing them the costly wars that drained English colonies.

stimulus.attribution: Described from A.J. Russell's 1869 photograph of the Golden Spike ceremony at Promontory Summit, Utah.
stimulus.text: The 1869 photograph of the Golden Spike ceremony at Promontory Summit, Utah, shows two locomotives nose to nose, surrounded by celebrating workers and officials — the moment the continent was joined by rail.

parts: A. Briefly explain ONE way American settlement rapidly transformed the West in the 25 years after the Civil War.
B. Briefly explain a SECOND such transformation.
C. Briefly explain ONE way Native Americans resisted American settlement in this period.
exemplar: The transcontinental railroad, completed at Promontory Summit in 1869, let settlers, cattle, and wheat move cheaply across the continent, knitting the West to eastern markets.
The Homestead Act (1862) offered 160 acres of public land to settlers, drawing hundreds of thousands of farms onto the Plains.

Native peoples resisted fiercely: the Sioux destroyed Custer's command at Little Bighorn (1876), and the Ghost Dance movement sought spiritual renewal against white expansion before it was crushed at Wounded Knee (1890).
